The head of the UN’s International Maritime Organization said the plan to move stranded ships out of the Persian Gulf through the strait will be on hold until the agency can confirm safety guarantees for the ships on the evacuation list and in the region.

The United Nations has put a pause on its effort to evacuate more than 11,000 sailors trapped in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran raised objections to the plan and a cargo ship was attacked near Oman. The sudden pause, along with the attack, shows just how fragile traffic through one of the busiest shipping corridors in the world remains, even after the US and Iran reached a truce. The UN's International Maritime Organization had only announced its evacuation plan on Tuesday. Dominguez noted that several ships had already been evacuated successfully under the plan before the pause. He explained that he wants to use this time to reconfirm that proper safety guarantees are still in place, both for vessels on the evacuation list and for everyone else currently in the region.

The IMO was helping evacuate hundreds of ships out of the strait, where they have been stranded for months. (West Asia News Agency via Reuters) The UN has paused its operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz after a vessel reported an attack. US officials said Iran fired on the ship, while Iran's strait authority said vessels outside routes it had set would not be guaranteed safe passage. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters earlier this week that if Iran threatened or blocked ships in the strait, "then we're going to have a problem". The UN International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has paused its operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz after a vessel reported an attack, reigniting fears for a preliminary deal to end the Iran war.

[Lähde: The Guardian World]
International Maritime Organization says plan on hold until safety guarantees confirmed after projectile hits vessel

A United Nations agency paused the evacuation of ships through the strait of Hormuz on Thursday after the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman following the passage of several tankers that used a route backed by the UN.

The head of the UN’s International Maritime Organization said the plan to move stranded ships out of the Persian Gulf through the strait will be on hold until the agency can confirm safety guarantees for the ships on the evacuation list and in the region.

It was unclear who launched the projectile or the type of vessel that was targeted. The report of a strike came hours after Iran threatened vessels to stop using the route through the strait without Tehran’s permission.

The vessel that was attacked was not part of the evacuation effort, said Arsenio Dominguez, the UN agency’s secretary-general.

After reports of the attack, Iran’s Persian Gulf strait authority – a new government agency established to control shipping in the strait – wrote on X that transit outside its own designated routes “will not be covered by the guarantee of safe passage”.

The UK Maritime Trade Operations centre said the vessel sustained damage, but it reported no injuries or environmental effects from the attack off the coast of Oman.

The opening of an alternative passage through the vital waterway would relieve pressure on the world economy and remove Iran’s main source of leverage in ongoing peace talks with the United States. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, on a visit to the Gulf to reassure American allies, said Washington was committed to the new route and ensuring that ships are able to transit the strait.

“If that stops, then we’re going to have a problem,” Rubio said Thursday before the report of the strike on the ship.

Traffic through the strait increased in recent days but was still well below prewar levels. Oil on Thursday briefly dipped below its last prewar price of just under $73 per barrel, a sign that the market believes the situation is improving.

The US and Iran are still debating terms of an interim peace deal, including issues such as getting ships through the narrow mouth of the Persian Gulf and addressing the future of Iran’s stockpile of highly enriched uranium.

---

US officials said Iran fired on the ship, while Iran's strait authority said vessels outside routes it had set would not be guaranteed safe passage.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio told reporters earlier this week that if Iran threatened or blocked ships in the strait, "then we're going to have a problem".

The UN International Maritime Organisation (IMO) has paused its operation to escort ships through the Strait of Hormuz after a vessel reported an attack, reigniting fears for a preliminary deal to end the Iran war.

The cargo ship said it was hit by a projectile while close to Oman, British navy agency UKMTO reported.

Two US officials told Reuters that Iran had fired on the ship, while Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority, which Tehran established to manage requests for ships to travel through the strait, said vessels outside routes it had set would not be guaranteed safe passage.

Four sources identified the ship as the Singapore-flagged Ever Lovely, which a security source said was likely targeted by a drone.

There was no immediate comment from the United States government.

US President Donald Trump warned earlier this month that, if Iran did not honour an agreement aimed at ending the war and reopening the strait, the US would probably go back to bombing the country again.

payload.title: YK keskeytti alusten evakuoinnit Hormuzinsalmessa hyökkäyksen jälkeen
payload.summary: YK:n alainen merenkulkujärjestö IMO on pysäyttänyt operaation, jolla aluksia ja miehistöjä oli määrä saattaa pois Persianlahdelta Hormuzinsalmen kautta. Päätös tehtiin sen jälkeen, kun aluksen kerrottiin joutuneen hyökkäyksen kohteeksi Omanin rannikon edustalla.
payload.content:
YK:n kansainvälinen merenkulkujärjestö IMO on keskeyttänyt alusten evakuoinnit Hormuzinsalmen kautta sen jälkeen, kun aluksen kerrottiin joutuneen hyökkäyksen kohteeksi Omanin rannikon edustalla. Järjestön mukaan operaatio voi jatkua vasta, kun turvallisuustakuut on varmistettu sekä evakuointilistalla oleville aluksille että muille alueella liikkuville.

## Evakuointisuunnitelma jäi tauolle

IMO oli auttamassa aluksia pois Persianlahdelta Hormuzinsalmen kautta. Lähdetietojen mukaan salmeen oli jäänyt jumiin satoja aluksia, ja tilanteen kerrottiin koskevan yli 11 000 merimiestä. Osa aluksista oli jo ehditty evakuoida onnistuneesti YK:n tukemaa reittiä pitkin ennen kuin operaatio pysäytettiin.

Keskeytys tehtiin torstaina sen jälkeen, kun Britannian armeija kertoi alukseen osuneen ammuksen Omanin rannikon edustalla. Toisissa tiedoissa kohteeksi kuvattiin rahtialus. Yhdysvaltalaisviranomaiset sanoivat Iranin tulittaneen alusta, kun taas Iranin salmiviranomainen oli ilmoittanut, ettei sen määrittämien reittien ulkopuolella kulkeville aluksille voida taata turvallista kulkua.

IMO:n pääsihteeri Arsenio Dominguez sanoi haluavansa käyttää tauon sen varmistamiseen, että asianmukaiset turvallisuustakuut ovat edelleen voimassa. Tarkistus koskee sekä evakuointilistalla olevia aluksia että muita alueella olevia aluksia ja miehistöjä.

## Hormuzinsalmen liikenne herättää huolta

IMO oli ilmoittanut evakuointisuunnitelmastaan vasta tiistaina. Iranin esittämien vastalauseiden ja Omanin edustalla raportoidun hyökkäyksen jälkeen suunnitelma on kuitenkin toistaiseksi pysäytetty. Lähteiden mukaan useita tankkereita oli ehtinyt kulkea YK:n tukemaa reittiä ennen uutta turvallisuusarviota.

Hormuzinsalmi on yksi maailman vilkkaimmista merikuljetusten väylistä. Hyökkäys ja evakuointien keskeyttäminen osoittavat, kuinka haavoittuvana liikenne alueella edelleen nähdään, vaikka Yhdysvaltojen ja Iranin välillä oli kerrottu saavutetun aselepo.

Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeri Marco Rubio varoitti aiemmin viikolla, että jos Iran uhkaisi tai estäisi aluksia Hormuzinsalmessa, seurauksena olisi vakava ongelma. Tilanne on nostanut uudelleen esiin kysymyksen siitä, voidaanko salmen kautta kulkevien alusten turvallisuus varmistaa ennen evakuointien jatkamista.

Tauko tehtiin sen jälkeen, kun aluksen kerrottiin joutuneen hyökkäyksen kohteeksi Omanin rannikon edustalla.
IMO aikoo varmistaa turvallisuustakuut ennen kuin operaatio voi jatkua.
payload.journalist_note: Artikkeli perustuu valitun lähdepaketin yhteneviin tietoihin. Iranin väitettyä osuutta koskeva kohta on muotoiltu viranomaisväitteeksi, koska lähteissä on eri osapuolten lausuntoja eikä riippumatonta vahvistusta hyökkääjästä.

Yhdysvaltain ulkoministeri Marco Rubio varoitti aiemmin viikolla, että jos Iran uhkaisi tai estäisi aluksia Hormuzinsalmessa, seurauksena olisi vakava ongelma. International Maritime Organization says plan on hold until safety guarantees confirmed after projectile hits vessel A United Nations agency paused the evacuation of ships through the strait of Hormuz on Thursday after the British military said a vessel was hit by a projectile off the coast of Oman following the passage of several tankers that used a route backed by the UN. The head of the UN’s International Maritime Organization said the plan to move stranded ships out of the Persian Gulf through the strait will be on hold until the agency can confirm safety guarantees for the ships on the evacuation list and in the region.

The United Nations has put a pause on its effort to evacuate more than 11,000 sailors trapped in the Strait of Hormuz after Iran raised objections to the plan and a cargo ship was attacked near Oman. The sudden pause, along with the attack, shows just how fragile traffic through one of the busiest shipping corridors in the world remains, even after the US and Iran reached a truce. The UN's International Maritime Organization had only announced its evacuation plan on Tuesday. He explained that he wants to use this time to reconfirm that proper safety guarantees are still in place, both for vessels on the evacuation list and for everyone else currently in the region.
